issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template (Main.java usage) expect a no-argument method messageOnRide(): String, but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implementations (Pig, Seal) use that parameter. This mismatch will confuse students about the required method signature and prevents compiling/using the solution API as described in the exercise text and template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent with the problem statement and template. Either remove the equipment parameter from the solution's Rideable interface and update Pig/Seal implementations to messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or update the problem statement and template (Main.java) to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and show examples calling it with an equipment argument. Preferably remove the extra parameter in the solution to match the exercise specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning the string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution introduces a different signature messageOnRide(String equipment) (and implementations that include the equipment in the returned string). This discrepancy between the expected no-arg messageOnRide() and the solution's parameterized method breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description and the template Main usage (which calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments) to the provided solution implementation, creating confusion and preventing straightforward implementation or testing.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide to the no-argument signature: String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal implementations to implement messageOnRide() returning exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template Main to reflect and call the parameterized method consistently.
